name: Bash
summary: The GNU project's Bourne-compatible Unix shell and command language: a superset of the POSIX Shell Command Language adding indexed and associative arrays, [[ ]] conditional expressions, extended globbing, brace expansion, process substitution, coprocesses, namerefs and programmable completion. Default interactive shell on most Linux distributions.
standards: POSIX.1-2024 Shell Command Language (XCU chapter 2) - Bash in POSIX mode targets it

level_notes.0: GNU Bash (maintained by Chet Ramey on git.savannah.gnu.org) is the only complete implementation and the de facto definition of everything beyond POSIX. Bash-compatible re-implementations: Oils OSH (Python/C++), brush (Rust), mvdan/sh (Go parser and interpreter). Savannah cgit sometimes answers 502 to automated clients; links follow its stable /cgit/bash.git/tree/<path> scheme.
level_notes.1: No standard for Bash itself. The Bash Reference Manual (Texinfo, also bash(1)) is the official reference; POSIX XCU chapter 2 defines the subset Bash follows in POSIX mode (see the posix-sh entry). The NEWS/CHANGES files and the POSIX/COMPAT notes document semantics changes per release.
level_notes.2: Greg Wooledge's wiki (BashGuide, BashFAQ, BashPitfalls), the Bash Hackers Wiki (archived copy), the Advanced Bash-Scripting Guide (dated, use with care) and Chet Ramey's AOSA chapter on the implementation.
level_notes.3: Wikipedia, PLDB, Hyperpolyglot shell comparison; Rosetta Code files Bash under the UNIX Shell category.
